Graphs of a Fitted Model

Source: R/plot_core.R
autoplot.StatmodFit.Rd

autoplot() returns a ggplot2 object that shows one aspect of a StatmodFit(), and plot() prints that object and returns it invisibly. The graph is chosen by plot_type, an object inheriting from plot_type:

  • with term, a graph of that term (plot_effect() when plot_type is not given, or the term's default_plot());

  • with a model_plot or a diagnostic_plot type, a graph of the whole fit, for which term and param are not given;

  • with neither, the four diagnostic graphs of diagnostics() composed in one figure.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'StatmodFit'
autoplot(
  object,
  term = NULL,
  param = NULL,
  plot_type = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  legend = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'StatmodFit'
plot(
  x,
  term = NULL,
  param = NULL,
  plot_type = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  legend = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object, x

A StatmodFit().

term

The name of a term or of a variable, a single string, or NULL.

param

The name of an equation (a parameter of the family), or NULL.

plot_type

An object inheriting from plot_type, or NULL.

data

The data frame of the fit, or NULL.

legend

NULL, TRUE or FALSE. NULL leaves each graph with the property legend of its type; TRUE or FALSE sets it on every graph drawn, the four diagnostic graphs included, so that plot(fit, legend = FALSE) draws them without legends.

...

Unused.

Value

autoplot() returns a ggplot2 object (a patchwork object for the composed diagnostics); plot() returns the same object invisibly, after printing it.

Details

term is the name of a term as summary.StatmodFit() prints it (spaces are ignored, so "random(~1|id)" names random(~1 | id)), or the name of a variable. A variable selects every term of the equation in which it appears and, within the linear part, the columns that involve it, so that with y ~ x + s(x) the variable x draws the sum of the linear and the smooth contribution. param is the equation; it may be omitted when the term belongs to one equation only.

The fit does not keep its data, so a graph that reads the covariates (partial residuals, a grid over a covariate, residuals against a covariate) requires the fitting data as data, and signals an error without it.

The data of the graph are in the returned object (p$data of each layer, or ggplot2::layer_data()), and plot_data() returns them without the graph.

See also

plot_type for the list of graphs, diagnostics(), plot_data()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(150), z = rnorm(150))
dd$y <- sin(2 * pi * dd$x) + 0.5 * dd$z + rnorm(150, sd = 0.3)
fit <- statmod(y ~ z + s(x), distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
p <- ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "s(x)", data = dd)
p + ggplot2::labs(title = "The smooth of x")

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "z", plot_type = plot_effect(residuals = FALSE),
                  data = dd)
